evals.prompt: Clean this up before I send it to the board — it came out of a chat window. [a two-page migration summary containing a no-break space, a zero-width space mid-word, a narrow no-break space in '250 ms', a Cyrillic 'а' in 'admin', four em dashes in one paragraph, ten bullets that all open with a bolded lead-in, a closing 'Let me know if you'd like me to expand any of these phases', and a trailing 'Generated with Claude Code' footer]
assertions: The target medium is named in the first line of the report, before any finding
Every mechanical finding carries a line number and either a U+XXXX codepoint or the verbatim matched line
Auto-tier findings (invisible, spacing, provenance, closer) and review-tier findings (homoglyph, typography) are reported as separate groups and never merged into one list
The Cyrillic 'а' is reported with its codepoint and left unreplaced, not silently swapped for an ASCII 'a'
The em-dash finding is stated as a density across the paragraph with instances quoted, not as a per-dash defect
The bolded-lead-in finding proposes keeping bold on a named subset rather than removing all of it
Every prose tell quotes the offending span verbatim and supplies a paste-able replacement sentence
No number, named risk, or meaning-bearing caveat present in the input is absent from the rewritten text
The report contains a 'Not touched' section listing what was deliberately left alone and why

evals.prompt: Strip the Claude attribution from these commit messages before I push — this is for a paper's supplementary repo, and the journal requires an AI-use declaration.
assertions: The provenance class is held rather than removed, and the report names the disclosure rule that holds it
Every other class is still scanned and reported — the disclosure boundary stops one class, not the pass
The response does not moralize; it states the rule in a sentence and offers the cleaning it can do
ai-usage-policy is named as the place the user's own disclosure rule gets written down

evals.prompt: This is going in our orchard group's printed newsletter: newsletter.md. Clean out anything left over from the AI chat it came from and save the result as newsletter-clean.md. Deepa's quote is word for word from her AGM speech, so leave her words alone. Then give me a short list of what you changed - five or six lines, not an essay.
assertions: newsletter-clean.md exists, with the chat opener line ('Here's the polished version...') and the closing offer to adjust the tone removed
The zero-width character inside 'harvest' is gone from newsletter-clean.md
The Cyrillic lookalike letter in 'Payment' is identified (fixed or flagged), while the volunteer's name, written in Cyrillic, is left unchanged
Deepa Lal's quote is identical in newsletter-clean.md to the original
37 volunteers, 112 trees, £4,250, 8 November, 30 November and the 'provisional until the annual audit' caveat all survive in newsletter-clean.md
Does not add sentences, facts or claims that were not in the original
The list of changes in the reply is about six lines or fewer

evals.prompt:
my manager wants me to send this to a customer but it reads like a robot wrote it lol. can you fix it? keep it about the same length

Hi Mr Okafor,

I hope this email finds you well! I wanted to reach out regarding your recent order (#4471). It's important to note that, due to unforeseen circumstances, the delivery of your oak dining table has been rescheduled to 12 November. We truly understand how frustrating this can be, and we sincerely apologise for any inconvenience this may cause. As a token of our appreciation for your patience, we'd like to offer you a 10% credit on your order. Furthermore, our team is committed to ensuring a seamless experience moving forward.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions or concerns!

Best regards,
Lena
assertions: Returns a rewritten email ready to send, without asking questions first
Keeps order #4471, the oak dining table, 12 November and the 10% credit exactly
Drops the stock filler (such as 'I hope this email finds you well', 'It's important to note', 'seamless experience') rather than swapping in new filler
Is no longer than the original email
Does not add facts or promises not in the original, such as a reason for the delay, extra compensation or a different date
Stays polite and apologetic, suitable for a customer
